title: Empowered Democrats Set Sights on Elon Musk, Stephen Miller, and Corporate America Following Midterm Sweep
snippet: Fresh off a decisive midterm election victory, incoming Democratic congressional leaders are preparing aggressive investigations into top Trump administration officials, billionaire Elon Musk, and corporate bad actors.
content:
WASHINGTON — Following a sweeping midterm victory that flipped control of Congress, Capitol Hill Democrats are wasting no time laying the groundwork for a barrage of aggressive investigations targeting key allies of President Donald Trump, top White House officials, and corporate entities.

Appearing on Sunday morning talk shows, incoming Democratic leaders signaled a sharp pivot toward oversight when the new Congress convenes in January, pointing to tech billionaire Elon Musk and newly appointed White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller as prime targets for subpoenas and public hearings.

Focus on Musk, Miller, and Wall Street

Representative Robert Garcia of California, slated to lead the House Oversight Committee, made clear that Musk's recent role in mass federal workforce layoffs under the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) will face intense scrutiny. "I think there's a lot of interest, not just from our committee, but from committees across the Congress to speak to Mr. Musk," Garcia said during an interview on CNN's "State of the Union."

Garcia also highlighted plans to investigate Miller, describing him as the central architect behind the administration's controversial immigration crackdown. Despite growing public pushback—including a drop in Trump's immigration approval rating to 37% following deadly enforcement operations in Minnesota—Miller's recent promotion to Chief of Staff signals the White House intends to double down on its hardline stance.

Meanwhile, Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, set to chair the Senate Banking Committee, issued a stern warning to corporate America. Speaking on CBS's "Face the Nation," Warren warned that companies profiting by "cheating American families and scamming your investors" should brace for serious congressional probes.

Impeachment Push Against Hegseth

In addition to committee probes, incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries confirmed Democrats are ready to back an impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The effort, initiated by outgoing Republican Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky, stems from mounting frustration over Hegseth's management of the military conflict in Iran, which has driven a sharp spike in domestic gas prices.

Jeffries declared himself a "hard yes" on the measure during an appearance on ABC's "This Week," stating flatly, "Pete Hegseth has got to go."

Justice Department Signals Resistance

The incoming oversight offensive met immediate pushback from the administration. Attorney General Todd Blanche signaled on Sunday that the Justice Department is fully prepared to clash with congressional Democrats, calling threats against White House personnel intolerable.

"If that's what this new incoming leadership wants to do, we are ready," Blanche said. "If you work in this administration, you have a lawyer. It's me."
